title: Sonia Bompastor breaks her silence on whether Chelsea will take disciplinary action against Sam Kerr after the Matildas star was cleared of racially aggravated harassment
text:
Chelsea’s manager, Sonia Bompastor, has revealed that the club will not take any disciplinary measure against Sam Kerr, stating that her apology ‘was enough’.
It occurs after the 31 -year -old was authorized by racially aggravated harassment of a police officer on Tuesday.
Kerr, who has played for Chelsea since 2019, had called PC Stephen Lovell ‘Stupid and White’ after a heated discussion at the Twickenham police station in 2023.
The questions have also been increasing in recent days about whether Kerr will continue as captain of the national part of Australian women after trial.
Speaking to the media on Thursday before Chelsea’s match against Everton this weekend, Bompastor said the club would meet in Kerr.
“I think, as you can imagine, it was a difficult week, a difficult week for her and her family,” said Chelsea coach during a press conference on Thursday.
Sam Kerr was photographed in training for the first time since he was authorized as racially aggravated harassment
Before Chelsea’s clash with Everton this weekend, the head of the Blues, Sonia Bompastor, confirmed that Chelsea would not take disciplinary measures against Sam Kerr
B “
‘Sam made a statement, apologized for that and I think that is enough.
‘Sometimes you can make mistakes. All, all women can make mistakes. It is what you learn from that and how you advance. But when you know the person who knows he is really kind and may be a moment in his life where something happened and if he has to reflect on that, he will probably say: “I don’t want to go through that.” ‘
Bompastor then declared that the club was only interested in launching its support behind Kerr after the conclusion of the trial.
“Yes, it happens in life and now you must also be forgiven for that and advance,” he said.
‘But I think he made a statement and it was clear in his statement, it was clear in his statement and I think that was clear enough. I think what he faced last week was difficult enough for her.
“The only thing we want to do as a club is to support it.”
She emphasized the importance of supporting Kerr in the coming weeks, adding: ‘We care about Sam and we just want to do our best.
‘Since I joined Chelsea, I met Sam as a player and person, and I was very surprised that she participated in that. Who is she does not reflect what I heard in court and what I was reading in the newspapers.
“Sam acknowledged that sometimes you can make mistakes,” he added.
Sam Kerr was authorized by racially aggravated harassment of a police officer on Tuesday and was photographed Thursday in training for Chelsea
Chelsea striker and Australia called a “stupid and white” police officer “during a heated discussion at the Twickenham police station in January 2023
Since then, he has issued an apology and has reaffirmed that he had not “tried to insult or harm anyone”
‘But from what I know about her, she is a very pleasant person.
‘It’s hard for me to understand why it was like that and why he had to spend a week in court. But it is.
“The most important thing is that you can see the future and now not think about that.”
Chelsea manager revealed that he had been in contact with Kerr throughout the judicial process, which lasted seven days and concluded Tuesday afternoon.
‘I think it is always important to show support to your players. I think Sam felt the support of the entire club, all his teammates and his staff, ” said Blues manager.
‘We, probably with her family, are the ones who know her most. And yes, it was difficult to see her in that situation. We are a family and we are really supporting it and I am very happy that the verdict has been positive and now it can advance. ‘
Bompastor gave an update on how Kerr has been in the days after the trial.
“I think she has stayed the same,” Bompastor said. ‘She did not change her behavior or mentality. I think it is a really difficult situation to face and I was probably not proud, but yes, it is.
Bompastor could not give a time frame of when Kerr would play again, with the star of the blues shown in the training on Thursday
Kerr has not played football for more than a year, with Chelsea striker ‘making good progress’ according to Bompastor
‘You know when you know Sam, he is a very shy person and wants to live his life in the light. He is a really normal person and likes to be quiet. This type of week for her was something big.
“But she just wants to be a normal person and likes to be normal.”
After the conclusion of the trial, Kerr issued a statement in which he thanked his family members for their support, but declared that he had not wanted to insult or harm anyone.
“After today’s non -guilty verdict, I can finally leave this challenging period behind,” said Chelsea star on Tuesday night.
‘While I apologize for expressing myself badly in what was a traumatic night, I have always argued that I did not intend to insult or harm anyone and I am grateful that the jury agreed unanimously.
“I would like to thank my partner Kristie, my family, my friends and all fans for their love and support, especially those who attended the Court every day.”
Kerr and his fiancee Kristie Mewis announced last November that they were waiting for a baby, with the Blues striker revealing during the trial of last week waiting for a baby.
He also revealed that she and Mewis had planned to marry in December.
Kerr had also declared that he hoped to focus on his family and football after trial, with her and her fiance Mewis waiting for a baby this year
Kerr added: “I am completely focused on returning to the field and I look forward to an exciting year for me and my family.”
Earlier on Thursday, Kerr went to Instagram to publish multiple photos of herself smiling while returning to Chelsea training.
Matildas captain has been marginalized for more than a year with a LCA injury and, according to Bompastor, advances while offering to return.
Bompastor gave an update on when Kerr could return to action for blues, after having suggested that he could return in February or in March.
“It’s hard to give a really precise period of time for Sam,” said Bompastor.
‘Really happy to have her back in the field with us with the team. She is not practicing completely with the team and is still being handled and is really individual, each player is different, but it is different to give a frame of time.
“He is progressing with his rehabilitation and going in the right direction.”
Bompastor comments come after Football Australia (FA) also gave their support to Chelsea striker.
But the governing body did not reveal whether the 31 -year -old will keep the captain’s bracelet.
“Football Australia recognizes today’s non -guilty verdict about Sam Kerr and welcomes Sam’s statement,” FA said in Wednesday’s statement.
‘Sam has been a key figure in Australian football for many years, and we recognize the significant pressures that this matter has brought to Sam, Kristie, his family and all those involved, including the impact he has had on the game.
Football Australia has also declared that they will continue to support Kerr in the coming weeks, but they have not commented if Matildas captaincy will keep
‘Throughout this period, Football Australia has remained committed to supporting Sam and will continue to do so while focusing on his football career, the rehabilitation of an injury and the return to play.
‘Football Australia invests a lot in the construction of the standards and behavior expectations of all involved with our game, especially for all our players of the national team, where leadership comes with additional responsibilities inside and outside the field.
‘Football Australia will be reflected with Sam on the learning of this matter and we will continue to provide adequate support for its progress.
“We expect Sam’s return to the countryside and his continuous contributions to both his club and the Matildas on the world stage.”
